<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes the encoder-cache deadlock with a drafter look-ahead (EAGLE / MTP) reported in the second half of #40707 ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40707#issuecomment-5760731067)). When two multimodal items only fit in the encoder cache one at a time and the gap between them is smaller than `2 * num_prefill_lookahead`, the request hangs forever, getting 0 scheduled tokens on every step with no error or log. The Mamba-alignment half of #40707 was already fixed by #51603.

## Claims

- A request with adjacent multimodal items that can't share the encoder cache now finishes under speculative decoding instead of hanging. Before this change it hung whenever `gap < 2 * L`, where `L = num_prefill_lookahead`.
- Output doesn't change. With temperature 0 the text matches the no-spec baseline exactly, and no `Encoder cache miss` was observed.

## Validation

**E2E** (1x GB200, MRV2, async scheduling on, prefix caching off): `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B`, MTP with `num_speculative_tokens=1` (L=1). Each request has two 3008x4032 images of 11844 tokens each; the encoder cache is 16384, so only one image fits at a time. I used raw prompts to control how many tokens sit between the two `<|image_pad|>` runs, and confirmed the placeholder offsets in the scheduler (gap=0 gives `[(4, 11844), (11848, 11844)]`).

| | gap=0 | gap=1 | gap=2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, MTP | **hang** (no completion in 300 s) | **hang** | OK |
| this PR, MTP | OK (2 runs) | OK | OK |
| main, no spec (baseline) | OK | OK | OK |

At temperature 0, every OK run with this PR produces the same text as the no-spec baseline for the same prompt: "The first image contains a red circle, and the second image contains a blue rectangle." MTP acceptance was 9/9 drafts in all spec runs.

<details>
<summary>Scheduler-level sweep (L x gap; image=600 tokens, cache=900)</summary>

| L \ gap | 0 | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (main) | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok |
| 1 (main) | hang | hang | ok | ok | ok |
| 3 (main) | hang | hang | hang | hang | ok |
| 1, 3 (this PR) | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok |

#59030 at `17d95d3eb8` gives the same results as main in this sweep.
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** Two places offset by the drafter look-ahead `L`, in opposite directions:

1. `_free_encoder_inputs` keeps item 1 until `num_computed_tokens >= end1 + L`. This was added in #46315.
2. When item 2 can't be allocated, `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs` stops the chunk at `start2 - L`.

If `start2 - L < end1 + L`, then `num_computed_tokens` can never reach the point where item 1 is freed, so item 2 is never allocated.

**Fix.** Remove the `L` offset in both places:

- **Free** once `end <= num_computed_tokens - num_output_placeholders`, as without spec decode. Both the V1 and V2 gathers read the drafter window `[c + 1, c + k + 1)`, which is ahead of `num_computed_tokens`. Once the target has passed an item, neither the target nor the drafter reads it again. Rejection rollback is still covered by `num_output_placeholders`. Async scheduling has the same timing as the existing non-spec path.
- **Stop at `start2`** instead of `start2 - L`, and only in the `can_allocate` failure branch. The drafter's read-ahead then lands on the item that isn't encoded yet. Both runners already handle that case: they fall back to token embeddings via the `start_pos >= computed + scheduled` check added in #46315. The `disable_chunked_mm_input` rollback still applies the shift.

Both changes are needed. Either one alone only narrows the hang condition from `gap < 2L` to `gap < L`.

**Tradeoff.** When the cache is full, the drafter uses token embeddings instead of image embeddings for up to `L` positions at that chunk boundary. This can slightly lower acceptance for one step. Requests whose items fit in the cache are unaffected.

**Relation to #59030.** #59030 adds a mid-schedule release of a request's consumed inputs, but it keeps the `+L` retention margin (its last commit re-added it). That release can never fire at this deadlock point, which is why its results match main in the sweep above. This PR instead argues that the margin isn't needed. The requeue half of #59030 is independent of this PR and complementary to it.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for analysis, the patch, tests, and running the validation. I reviewed every changed line and the results above.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

nodes.body: Thanks @gty111, splitting it makes sense. I checked 6d8d50d47 on CPU: the test from #59030 passes 6/6, its parent 816173ca9 still sticks at 649/650 for lookahead 1 with gaps 0 and 1, and the encoder, lookahead and spec cases in tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py pass (52).

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

nit: should we keep this "draft lookahead ignoring freed multimodal features" invariant (which we do not test per se due to the now-removed unit test) as a separate unit test? Otherwise a future code change breaking this invariant may result in a hard crash without a CI failure I think.

     assert output.finish_reason == FinishReason.ERROR
 
 
-def test_free_encoder_inputs_defers_for_eagle_lookahead():
-    """With EAGLE speculative decoding, the encoder input is retained one extra
-    position so the drafter's +1 look-ahead mm-embedding gather (which reads one
-    position past the target's computed range) still finds it cached. This is
-    the primary mechanism that prevents the drafter "Encoder cache miss"; the
-    worker-side token-embedding fallback is only a backstop."""
-    scheduler = create_scheduler(model="llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf")

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("prefill_lookahead", [1, 3])
+def test_drafter_lookahead_encoder_cache_cap_makes_progress(prefill_lookahead):
+    """Regression test for #40707: with a drafter look-ahead, two adjacent
+    images that only fit in the encoder cache one at a time must not deadlock.
+    Stopping short of the second image by the look-ahead used to leave the
+    first image unfreed, so the second could never be allocated."""
+    image_len = 600
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(max_num_batched_tokens=900, max_model_len=2048)
+    scheduler.num_prefill_lookahead = prefill_lookahead
+    scheduler.max_num_encoder_input_tokens = 900
+    scheduler.encoder_cache_manager = EncoderCacheManager(cache_size=900)
+
+    num_tokens = 2 * image_len + 20
     request = create_requests(
         num_requests=1,
-        num_tokens=250,
-        mm_positions=mm_positions,
+        num_tokens=num_tokens,
+        mm_positions=[
+            [
+                PlaceholderRange(offset=10, length=image_len),
+                PlaceholderRange(offset=10 + image_len, length=image_len),
+            ]
+        ],
+        max_tokens=1,
+        req_ids=["req"],
     )[0]
-    manager = scheduler.encoder_cache_manager
-    manager.allocate(request, 0)
-    mm_end = 150  # offset + length
-
-    # Confirmed progress reaches the range end: without spec decode this frees
-    # (see test below), but the drafter's +1 look-ahead still needs it.
-    request.num_computed_tokens = mm_end
-    scheduler._free_encoder_inputs(request)
-    assert manager.get_cached_input_ids(request) == {0}
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
 
-    # One position past the range end: the +1 look-ahead has now passed it.
-    request.num_computed_tokens = mm_end + 1
-    scheduler._free_encoder_inputs(request)
-    assert manager.get_cached_input_ids(request) == set()
+    scheduled_inputs = []
+    while request.num_computed_tokens < num_tokens:
+        output = scheduler.schedule()
+        assert output.num_scheduled_tokens.get("req", 0) > 0
+        scheduled_inputs += output.scheduled_encoder_inputs.get("req", [])
+        scheduler.update_from_output(
+            output,
+            ModelRunnerOutput(
+                req_ids=["req"],
+                req_id_to_index={"req": 0},
+                sampled_token_ids=[[]],
+                logprobs=None,
+                prompt_logprobs_dict={},
+                pooler_output=[],
+            ),
+        )
+    assert scheduled_inputs == [0, 1]
